source.title: More is Less: Inducing Sparsity via Overparameterization
source.authors: Hung-Hsu Chou; J. Maly; Holger Rauhut

record.tranche_reason: Tests an implicit-bias claim with a sparse-recovery setting and recovery/optimization-error measures, rather than measuring train-to-test generalization on natural labels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports sparse-signal recovery experiments and a theoretical characterization of gradient flow. Its discussion of generalization and cited findings about overparameterized neural networks are introductory context, not measured outcomes. The recovery experiments bear on V4 only as results about vanilla gradient methods versus ℓ1 minimization; they do not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD. No supplied version directly covers sparse recovery.
record.test_reason: The study measures synthetic sparse-vector recovery and proximity to minimum ℓ1 norm, not any outcome named in V1–V8. It cites neural-network generalization findings as motivation. Its comparisons of factorized gradient descent, ordinary gradient descent and ℓ1 minimization do not test adaptive optimizers versus SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. More precisely, with positive initialization and a nonempty feasible set, factorized gradient flow converges to a feasible solution approximately minimizing an initialization-dependent signed weighted ℓ1 norm; uniform balanced initialization yields the ordinary ℓ1 case. This gives near-optimal sparse-recovery sampling guarantees under suitable measurement conditions. Numerical gradient-descent experiments resemble ℓ1 minimization and show an initialization accuracy–speed tradeoff; extending the theory to gradient descent remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes overparameterized Hadamard-factorized square loss for compressed sensing, using vanilla gradient flow theoretically and gradient descent experimentally; it does not test the natural-label generalization recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization magnitude changes the relative optimization error and convergence speed; depth changes the observed scaling of error with initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Factorized gradient descent achieves sparse-recovery probabilities similar to ℓ1 minimization; ordinary quadratic-loss gradient descent barely recovers until M = N.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hadamard-factorized square losses can induce an implicit sparsity bias in underdetermined linear recovery without explicit regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller initialization improves relative ℓ1 optimization error but requires more iterations. Error scaling is polynomial for L > 2 and logarithmic for L = 2; L = 2 converges fastest without achieving the best ℓ1 accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale and factorization depth control the accuracy and convergence speed of implicit ℓ1 minimization in sparse recovery.

record.peer_reviewed: Information and Inference: A Journal of the IMA
record.problems: The experimental results use gradient descent as an approximation to the theoretically analyzed gradient flow. Recovery plots are described qualitatively without numeric values or reported uncertainty. The experiments concern synthetic sparse recovery, not natural-label test generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on a listed version were reported. Introductory claims and cited results about natural-label generalization and overparameterization were excluded as prior-work context.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, held-out performance, tuning, weight decay and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out classifier error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining to measure test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2 classification conflicts with its own gate note. A different method qualifies as T2 only when it addresses a listed version's question; sparse recovery alone does not. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, while the recovery findings themselves are reported clearly.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test generalization.
Width sweeps and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on image or language benchmarks, including effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large-batch training and held-out performance under epoch budgets.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking a train-test generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Gradient descent on reduced factorized loss (equivalently, overparameterized loss when initializing identically)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on factorized loss to reconstruct nonnegative sparse vectors from Gaussian measurements.
rows.measure: Empirical probability of successful recovery; success defined by reconstruction error at most 1%.
rows.baseline: ℓ1 minimization with positivity constraint behaved similarly; exact numerical value not stated.
rows.note: The stated outcome is qualitative; the figure's recovery probabilities are not transcribed as numeric values.
rows.check: Recovery probability does not measure a listed version. Figure 2 reports separate factorized conditions L = 2 and L = 3, which this row pools. The iteration count is 10^7.

rows.subject: Gradient descent on regular quadratic loss
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on the regular quadratic loss for sparse-vector recovery.
rows.measure: Empirical probability of successful recovery; success defined by reconstruction error at most 1%.
rows.note: The text states that recovery is limited until the linear system is fully determined.
rows.check: Failure to reconstruct a sparse vector from underdetermined measurements is not absence or partial observation of any listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: Gradient descent on generalized overparameterized loss function
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on generalized overparameterized loss to reconstruct general signed ground-truth vectors.
rows.measure: Empirical probability of successful recovery; comparison described by recovery-probability plots.
rows.baseline: Standard ℓ1 minimization without positivity constraints; numeric value not stated.
rows.value: outcome is comparable to the positive-solution experiment; gradient descent on factorizations performs similarly to ℓ1-minimization
rows.note: No figure values are provided in the text.
rows.check: Sparse recovery does not measure a listed version. Figure 3 separates L = 2, 3 and 4, which this row pools.

rows.subject: Gradient descent on generalized overparameterized loss function, L = 2
rows.operation_detail: Compared relative optimization error across initialization magnitudes.
rows.value: accuracy improves as α decreases; convergence fastest among tested layer counts, but does not give the best results in ℓ1-minimization
rows.note: Qualitative trends are stated; no exact plotted error values are given.
rows.check: Relative ℓ1 optimization error is not held-out error or a generalization gap. Figure 4 reports logarithmic initialization scaling for L = 2; the row omits this distinction. Its accuracy wording refers to ℓ1 minimization.
